cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Replication lag is the delay between a write committing on the leader and becoming visible on a replica. It exists only with asynchronous or semi-synchronous replication.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: It is rarely the network. Causes: replica disk I/O, heavy read queries starving the replica, and single-threaded apply. Lag breaks read-your-writes, makes data appear to go backwards, and can lose data on failover. MySQL measures Seconds_Behind_Source; PostgreSQL uses pg_stat_replication.

questions.q: A user updates their profile, refreshes and sees the old one. Why?
questions.a: The refresh read a lagging replica, violating read-your-writes. Route that user's reads to the leader for a while.

questions.q: Is network RTT usually the cause of lag?
questions.a: No. It is the least common cause; disk I/O, heavy reads and single-threaded apply dominate.
To apply transactions in exactly the leader's order.
